title: 1INME — Sectioned Deck
description: Master cover for the 1INME multi-section deck.
speakerNotes: Open the deck. One identity, one platform — that's the whole pitch in a sentence. Tell the room which section you'll spend most of the time in, then jump straight there from the table of contents.

title: Table of contents
description: Each section is appendix-separated by a divider slide. Jump to the divider to start the section.
speakerNotes: Six sections, appendix-separated by dividers. Tell the audience to interrupt and pick whichever section matters most — the dividers act as bookmarks, so you can jump without losing your place.

title: Appendix · Sales presentation.
description: Section divider for the sales presentation block.
speakerNotes: Shift into the sales pitch. Twenty slides from problem to next step — feel free to skip the proof slides if the buyer is already convinced. Set expectations: this section ends with a concrete CTA.

title: The modern professional drowns in tools.
description: Bio links, scheduler, CRM, vault, analytics — none of them talking to each other.
speakerNotes: Open with the numbers behind the pain. Read the nine-tools stat first, let it sit, then move through cost, usage, and lost hours. The point: this is real money and real time bleeding out today, not a future risk.

title: What fragmentation actually costs.
description: What fragmentation actually costs.
speakerNotes: Translate the numbers into business cost. Hours, data, brand, revenue — frame each as something the buyer's team will feel this quarter, not abstractly someday. Pause after 'lost revenue' and ask which one stings most.

title: 1INME — the everything platform.
description: Identity, links, AI, productivity, and analytics in one place.
speakerNotes: Pivot to the 1INME answer. Identity, tools, AI, insight — four cards, one platform. Don't list features yet; sell the shape: one home instead of nine browser tabs.

title: Why 1INME, not the next bundle.
description: Why 1INME, not the next bundle.
speakerNotes: Pre-empt the 'why not just use a bundle?' objection. Native, beautiful, open, fair — these are the four things bundles structurally can't fake. Mention a competitor by name only if the buyer brings them up.

title: ROI of consolidating onto 1INME.
description: ROI of consolidating onto 1INME.
speakerNotes: Make the ROI math obvious: about $1,400 saved annually, six hours back per week, conversion lift, single invoice. Anchor the buyer to a payback window measured in weeks, not quarters.

title: Where the hours come back.
description: Time saved per week by switching to 1INME.
speakerNotes: Walk the time-savings table left to right. Bio maintenance, lead capture, cross-posting, reporting — call out the biggest win for the buyer's role first. Land the seven-hours-per-week footer total.

title: We replaced six tools and shaved a workday off every week. The team finally has one place to live.
description: We replaced six tools and shaved a workday off every week. The team finally has one place to live.
speakerNotes: Read the quote slowly. Pause on 'shaved a workday off every week'. Mention this is a real early-access customer and offer to set up a reference call after this meeting.

title: Loved by early teams across creator, coaching, and agency.
description: Replace these placeholders with real logos and case studies as deals close.
speakerNotes: If logos are still placeholders, acknowledge it and skip ahead. Otherwise, point to the closest analogue to the buyer in the room — same size, same vertical — and offer to introduce them.

title: What customers measure after 90 days.
description: What customers measure after 90 days.
speakerNotes: Frame these as 90-day expectations, not promises. Six tools removed and a 24% lift in lead-to-close are the lines that move buying committees — repeat them twice.

title: Pricing, at a glance.
description: Pick the plan that matches the team you have today.
speakerNotes: Anchor on Studio first — most teams land here. Free is for evaluation, Pro is for power individuals, Business is for compliance and scale. Call out the 20% annual discount before someone asks.

title: What buyers ask, and how we answer.
description: The four objections we hear most often — and the proof points to handle them.
speakerNotes: Run the four objections proactively. The buyer is already thinking them; saying them out loud builds trust. Keep each answer to one sentence and move on.

title: How 1INME compares.
description: How 1INME compares.
speakerNotes: Position relative to the specific tool the buyer mentioned in discovery. We're additive to most of these and replacing one or two — be honest about which is which.

title: Built so legal and IT can say yes.
description: Built so legal and IT can say yes.
speakerNotes: This is the slide for IT and legal — slow down here if either is in the room. MFA, SSO, SCIM, audit, SOC 2 trajectory. Offer the evidence pack on request.

title: What buyers see on day one.
description: A single dashboard that proves the value within the first hour.
speakerNotes: Show what the buyer's workspace looks like on day one — not in three months. Live bio page, trained companion, imported pipeline, working funnel. The point: time-to-value is hours.

title: Three buyer outcomes we underwrite.
description: Three buyer outcomes we underwrite.
speakerNotes: Three outcomes we underwrite. Pick the one that matches the buyer's stated goal from discovery and spend most of the slide there. Skim the other two unless asked.

title: What the first 30 days look like.
description: What the first 30 days look like.
speakerNotes: Walk the four-week plan. The point is predictability: by the end of week four the ROI snapshot is in their inbox, not promised vaguely for 'soon'.

title: Where buyers see early proof.
description: Where buyers see early proof.
speakerNotes: Customer stories — replace placeholders with the closest real match before sending. Lead each card with the result, then the customer name. If you don't have a story, leave the card off.

title: Our buyer-side guarantees.
description: Our buyer-side guarantees.
speakerNotes: These four risk-removers are designed to make 'yes' the safe answer. 30-day money-back is the headline; mention white-glove migration is included free on Studio and up.

title: Recommended next steps.
description: Recommended next steps.
speakerNotes: Tell the buyer exactly what happens next. The four-step ladder gives them an easy first 'yes' — start with the 30-minute walkthrough and book it before you leave the call.

title: Sales CTA
description: Sales section call to action.
speakerNotes: Close. Pick a slot together on screen; don't leave with 'we'll send a calendar link' — that's where deals stall. Capture the email and book the next meeting live.

title: Appendix · Product presentation.
description: Twenty slides to walk a prospect through the full product surface.
speakerNotes: Shift into the product walkthrough. Twenty slides covering web, mobile, API, every module, and the platform layer. Tell the audience to flag the modules they want to go deep on.

title: What 1INME is, end to end.
description: One identity, three surfaces, eleven modules — wired together by AI and analytics.
speakerNotes: Set up the product walkthrough. Three surfaces, eleven modules, identity + vault + AI as the spine. Audience leaves this slide knowing the shape of the platform.

title: The web app.
description: The full-power workspace in your browser.
speakerNotes: Tour the web app: sidebar, drag-and-drop editor, AskCoach side panel, workspace switcher in the footer. Emphasise this is the full-power surface — everything works here first.

title: The mobile app.
description: A native companion for iOS and Android.
speakerNotes: Now the mobile app. NFC tap-to-share, smart dialer with deal context, voice capture between meetings, push notifications for leads and bookings. Designed for field work.

title: API & SDK.
description: Every capability is programmable.
speakerNotes: Show developers we're serious. Every capability is a REST endpoint with a webhook; SDK in TypeScript. Token-scoped and audit-logged. The mock is a real /v1/links call.

title: End-to-end user journey.
description: From first signup to first revenue, in one place.
speakerNotes: Walk signup → build → convert → operate. Time-to-value sits between steps two and three; brand kit detection at signup is the moment most prospects say 'oh, this is different'.

title: Cross-module workflows.
description: What happens when modules know about each other.
speakerNotes: Show what happens when modules know about each other. Bio → CRM, Smart Link → Pixel, Calendar → Vault, AI → everything. This is the slide that justifies the 'platform' word.

title: Identity is the spine.
description: Your handle is the entry point. Everything else inherits brand and permissions.
speakerNotes: Identity is what holds it together. Handle, SSO, brand kit, permissions — every other module inherits from here. Public surface vs. private surface is the mental model to leave them with.

title: Security & trust at the platform layer.
description: Security & trust at the platform layer.
speakerNotes: Re-state the security posture for a technical audience. MFA + passkeys, SSO + SCIM, encryption everywhere, full audit log. Same evidence pack as the sales conversation; offer it on request.

title: Admin & workspace overview.
description: Built for teams of every size.
speakerNotes: Show the admin surface. Workspaces per brand or client, role-based access on every module, white label per workspace, plan and seat management in one place.

title: Integrations map.
description: 1INME plugs into the tools you already use.
speakerNotes: Eight categories, top-of-mind tools per category. The point: 1INME doesn't pretend to be your CRM if you already have HubSpot — it sits beside it, two-way synced.

title: The onboarding flow.
description: Time-to-value measured in hours, not weeks.
speakerNotes: Detect, import, wire, launch. Time-to-value measured in hours, not weeks. We bring the data so day one is real, not a blank workspace.

title: Bio link pages.
description: The doorway to everything else.
speakerNotes: Open the module deep-dives with bio — the doorway to everything. Drag-and-drop blocks, themes, custom domains, AB tests built in. This is the module most prospects already know.

title: Smart short links.
description: Branded URLs with rules, pixels, and analytics.
speakerNotes: Smart links: routing rules, pixels, QR for every link. The intelligent layer between the click and the destination. Show the rules editor if you have time.

title: AI suite.
description: Companions, AskCoach, Voice, and Card Scanner.
speakerNotes: Companions, AskCoach, Voice, Card Scanner. Custom personalities, grounded in your Minds, hands-free on mobile. The differentiator vs. ChatGPT is grounding — say it explicitly.

title: Productivity & CRM.
description: Vault, Tasks, Forms, Calendar, CRM, Resume.
speakerNotes: One contact, one source of truth. Bookings tied to deals, vault under role-based access, tasks rolling up to the workspace dashboard. The CRM you wish HubSpot was for a small team.

title: Social & community.
description: Native creator feed plus cross-posting.
speakerNotes: Native creator feed plus cross-posting. Members-only content, per-platform previews, best-time scheduling. Two surfaces in one — owned audience and rented audience.

title: Mobile-first tools.
description: NFC cards, smart dialer, on-the-go capture.
speakerNotes: Mobile-first tools: NFC card, dialer with deal context on screen, scanner straight to CRM, voice notes that sync. Built for people who close deals away from a desk.

title: Analytics & insights.
description: From impression to outcome, across every module.
speakerNotes: Funnels and audience views across every module. Workspace and brand splits. Exports and threshold alerts. The slide that proves we're a platform, not a bundle.

title: The platform promise.
description: The platform promise.
speakerNotes: Open, composable, honest, yours. The four principles we won't break — even when it costs us. Read each one slowly; this is how prospects remember the brand.

title: Product CTA
description: Product section call to action.
speakerNotes: Close the product section. Offer a tailored demo on the modules they actually care about. Capture the next slot before leaving the call — same playbook as the sales close.

title: Appendix · Investor pitch.
description: Twenty slides for investor conversations. Numbers are placeholders unless tagged otherwise.
speakerNotes: Shift into the investor pitch. Twenty slides — vision, market, model, traction, ask. Anything tagged 'placeholder' must be replaced with live numbers before sending this section out.

title: Investor cover
description: Investor deck cover slide.
speakerNotes: Open the investor deck. State the thesis in one breath: identity-first everything platform for the creator economy. This is a Series A teaser — set expectations for figures up front.

title: Vision.
description: Replace fragmented tooling with a single identity-first platform for every creator and team.
speakerNotes: Three sentences for the vision. Identity is the new homepage. AI is the new operating system. One bill, one brand, one home. Don't elaborate; the next slides do that.

title: Problem.
description: Problem.
speakerNotes: Land the problem in numbers. Nine tools, $214 a month, 2.4 hours lost daily, 37% of features used. Note explicitly that these are placeholder market figures until the live research is in.

title: Market.
description: TAM / SAM / SOM placeholders.
speakerNotes: TAM / SAM / SOM. Be honest these are placeholders unless tagged otherwise — savvy investors will check. Replace with sourced figures (Statista, Gartner, internal) before sending.

title: Solution.
description: Identity, links, AI, productivity, and analytics — one platform.
speakerNotes: Three cards for the solution: surface, spine, modules. Resist the urge to go module-by-module here — the next sections do that. Land the 'one platform' shape and move on.

title: Product highlights.
description: Three demos investors remember.
speakerNotes: Tease the demo. Three moments investors remember: AskCoach grounded in your data, Smart Link wiring in one click, the cross-module funnel reveal. Five minutes total.

title: Business model.
description: Business model.
speakerNotes: Subscriptions, AI credit packs, white-label, affiliate. Four lines of revenue, tilted toward recurring SaaS. AI credits are the wedge into top-up revenue without surprise bills.

title: Pricing tiers.
description: Pricing tiers.
speakerNotes: Pricing tiers framed by investor narrative: acquisition (Free), highest LTV/CAC (Pro), modal price point (Studio), highest ARPA (Business). Studio is where most teams land.

title: Go-to-market.
description: Go-to-market.
speakerNotes: PLG + community + sales + affiliates. A distribution flywheel, not a single channel. Each one feeds the next: bio links go viral, creators refer creators, agencies bring teams.

title: Traction (placeholders).
description: Traction (placeholders).
speakerNotes: Replace placeholders with the latest numbers before sending. Mark the slide as confidential when you do. Lead with MoM growth — investors care about velocity more than absolutes early.

title: Competitive landscape.
description: Competitive landscape.
speakerNotes: Map ourselves against bio, links, CRM, AI. We're the only one with all four under a single identity layer. Avoid bashing competitors — frame us as the integration of their categories.

title: Moat.
description: Moat.
speakerNotes: Four moats: identity gravity, cross-module data, network effects, workspace lock-in. Each compounds the others — that's the slide-five-minutes-later answer for the partner meeting.

title: Team.
description: Replace placeholders with founder bios and pictures.
speakerNotes: Replace founder placeholders with bios and pictures before sending. Lead with prior outcomes, not titles. Investors back people first; product second.

title: Financials & projections (placeholders).
description: Replace with the live model before sending.
speakerNotes: Walk across rows: ARR, gross margin, NRR, burn multiple. Replace with the live model before sending. Investors will pull this into their own spreadsheet — make sure it ties out.

title: Funding ask.
description: Funding ask.
speakerNotes: Ask, equity, runway, post-money cap. Update with the live round structure before the meeting. Be ready to defend each number with a sentence.

title: Use of funds.
description: Use of funds.
speakerNotes: 40% product, 30% GTM, 20% customer success, 10% G&A. This is a build-and-distribute round, not a fix-and-survive one. Be specific about the first three engineering hires.

title: Milestones.
description: What we'll prove with this round.
speakerNotes: Quarterly milestones for the round — what we'll prove with this money. Pricing in Q1, AI in Q2, workspaces in Q3, mobile + enterprise in Q4. Each is dated and falsifiable.

title: Exit & long-term vision.
description: Exit & long-term vision.
speakerNotes: Three exit paths: strategic, growth, IPO. Don't oversell IPO — lead with credible strategic interest from adjacent platforms. Investors prefer optionality over a single bet.

title: Why now.
description: Why now.
speakerNotes: Four reasons this works in 2026 and didn't in 2022: AI credibility across workflows, tool fatigue at all-time highs, identity becoming the homepage, mobile parity finally possible.

title: Investor close
description: Investor pitch closing slide.
speakerNotes: Close the investor deck. Offer the live model, customer references, and a deeper product session. Confirm the next meeting on the call before hanging up.

title: Appendix · Future roadmap.
description: Twenty slides on what's coming, by horizon and by area.
speakerNotes: Shift into the roadmap section. Twenty slides organised as Now / Next / Later, broken down by area and rolled up by quarter. Be honest about what's GA versus directional.

title: How we plan the roadmap.
description: How we plan the roadmap.
speakerNotes: Frame how we plan: Now / Next / Later / Always. Set the expectation that quarters are the granularity, not weeks — that's a feature, not a bug.

title: Now / Next / Later — at a glance.
description: Now / Next / Later — at a glance.
speakerNotes: The full company roadmap on one slide. Now is shipping this quarter, Next is in active build, Later has direction set with details flexible. This is the slide most prospects screenshot.

title: Roadmap · AI.
description: Roadmap · AI.
speakerNotes: AI roadmap: Companions 2.0 now, AskCoach 3.0 next, an open Companion API later. Be honest about what's GA vs. directional — don't promise on-device inference yet.

title: Roadmap · Bio Links & Smart Links.
description: Roadmap · Bio Links & Smart Links.
speakerNotes: Bio + Smart Links roadmap. Editor v3 now, visual routing v3 next, programmable bios later. The marketplace for blocks is the long-tail bet here.

title: Roadmap · Productivity & CRM.
description: Roadmap · Productivity & CRM.
speakerNotes: Productivity & CRM roadmap. Pipeline 2.0 now, Vault sharing 2.0 next, Forms 2.0 later. This is where teams expand seats once they're on Studio.

title: Roadmap · Social & community.
description: Roadmap · Social & community.
speakerNotes: Social & community roadmap: cross-post v2 today, paid memberships next, community moments (live drops, polls, collabs) later. The members tier is the monetisation hook.

title: Roadmap · Mobile.
description: Roadmap · Mobile.
speakerNotes: Mobile roadmap: NFC v2 now, Smart Dialer 2.0 next, full mobile parity later. Apple Wallet pass is the headline announcement for this quarter.

title: Roadmap · Platform & API.
description: Roadmap · Platform & API.
speakerNotes: Platform & API roadmap. Webhook v2 with replay and signed payloads, GraphQL surface, in-product app store with partner-built modules. This is the developer-relations narrative.

title: Roadmap · Enterprise.
description: Roadmap · Enterprise.
speakerNotes: Enterprise roadmap: SSO + SCIM now (Okta, Azure AD, Google), workspace federation next, custom contracts (data residency, BYO key) later. The slide for the IT buyer.

title: Roadmap · Security & compliance.
description: Roadmap · Security & compliance.
speakerNotes: Security & compliance roadmap. SOC 2 Type II audit is active, ISO 27001 next with end-of-year target, regional data zones (EU, UK, APAC) later.

title: Roadmap · Internationalization.
description: Roadmap · Internationalization.
speakerNotes: i18n roadmap: localized UI in five languages today, local payments (SEPA, Pix, SPEI) next, region-specific content later. RTL is already supported.

title: Roadmap · Marketplace.
description: Roadmap · Marketplace.
speakerNotes: Marketplace roadmap: free templates today, paid templates with creator payouts next, full apps marketplace with revenue share later. This is the long-term platform play.

title: Roadmap · Analytics.
description: Roadmap · Analytics.
speakerNotes: Analytics roadmap: Funnels v2 with drag-and-drop steps, behavioural cohorts next, warehouse exports and BI partner connectors later.

title: Roadmap · Brand & design system.
description: Roadmap · Brand & design system.
speakerNotes: Brand & design system roadmap: per-workspace brand kits today, visual theme studio next, programmatic Design API later. The white-label foundation.

title: Roadmap · Integrations.
description: Roadmap · Integrations.
speakerNotes: Integrations roadmap: top 20 native today, top 50 next, the long tail covered via Zapier and Make. We won't build every connector ourselves — that's a feature.

title: Quarterly timeline.
description: What ships when, across the platform.
speakerNotes: Read this matrix across the rows, not down the columns. Investors and IT buyers care about pace per area — six themes shipping every quarter is the headline.

title: How we choose what to ship.
description: How we choose what to ship.
speakerNotes: Four principles for choosing what to ship: honest, open, realistic, bold. We commit to quarters, not weeks. Customers vote on the public roadmap — show them the URL.

title: Where the engineering hours go.
description: Where the engineering hours go.
speakerNotes: Where engineering hours go: 40% AI + integrations, 25% core modules, 20% platform + API, 15% performance and reliability. The split investors expect from a Series A platform.

title: How customers shape the roadmap.
description: How customers shape the roadmap.
speakerNotes: Four ways customers shape the roadmap: public requests, quarterly council, beta program, weekly office hours. The point: this isn't a closed roadmap — they have a seat at the table.

title: Roadmap close
description: Roadmap closing slide.
speakerNotes: Close the roadmap section. Invite them to vote on the public roadmap, join the customer council, or talk to product directly. One CTA — pick the one that fits the room.
